data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Topical antibacterials & antiseptics_

**Class:** Oxidising agent; antiseptic and astringent

## Mechanism of action
- Releases oxygen → oxidises organic matter; antibacterial and antifungal; astringent (dries weeping lesions)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Wet compresses and soaks for weeping/oozing dermatoses: acute eczema, pemphigus erosions, infected eczema, tinea pedis maceration, leg ulcers, bullous disorders
- Potassium permanganate baths

## Dose & formulations
- 1:10,000 solution (pale pink) — dissolve crystals fully; soak or compress for 10–15 min, once or twice daily for a few days

## Adverse effects
- Brown staining of skin and nails; burns and corrosive injury with concentrated solution or undissolved crystals; dryness
- Ingestion is toxic

## Contraindications
- Concentrated solutions; mucosa

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe.

## Viva points
- 1:10,000 pale pink solution — astringent for weeping lesions
- Undissolved crystals cause burns

_Sources: Khopkar ch.30 and ch.33 (Potassium permanganate bath). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
